name: CD

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      reason:
        description: "Reason for running manually"
        required: false
        default: "Testing"
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths-ignore:
      - "**/*.md"
      - "docs/**"
      - "LICENSE"
      - ".gitignore"
      - ".gitattributes"
      - ".github/CODEOWNERS"

env:
  REGISTRY: registry.ic-ops.net

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    name: Build and Push Docker Image
    runs-on: self-hosted-rocky-x64-16g
    outputs:
      rev_tag: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.rev_tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repo
        uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6.0.2

      - name: Generate image tag
        id: tag
        run: |
          REV_TAG="git-$(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD)"
          echo "rev_tag=$REV_TAG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Docker login
        uses: docker/login-action@b45d80f862d83dbcd57f89517bcf500b2ab88fb2 # v4.0.0
        with:
          registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
          username: ${{ vars.REGISTRY_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD }}

      - name: Set up BuildKit fleet
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@4d04d5d9486b7bd6fa91e7baf45bbb4f8b9deedd # v4.0.0
        with:
          name: eks-fleet
          driver: remote
          endpoint: tcp://buildkit-amd64-svc.buildkit-fleet.svc.cluster.local:4400
          platforms: linux/amd64
          append: |
            - endpoint: tcp://buildkit-arm64-svc.buildkit-fleet.svc.cluster.local:4400
              platforms: linux/arm64

      - name: Build and push
        uses: docker/build-push-action@bcafcacb16a39f128d818304e6c9c0c18556b85f # v7
        with:
          builder: eks-fleet
          push: true
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          tags: |
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/internal-tooling/churn-renewal-forecast:${{ steps.tag.outputs.rev_tag }}
            ${{ env.REGISTRY }}/internal-tooling/churn-renewal-forecast:latest
          cache-from: type=registry,ref=${{ env.REGISTRY }}/image-build-cache/internal-tooling/churn-renewal-forecast:cache
          cache-to: type=registry,ref=${{ env.REGISTRY }}/image-build-cache/internal-tooling/churn-renewal-forecast:cache,mode=max,image-manifest=true,ignore-error=true

      - name: Build overlays
        env:
          DEPLOY_DIR: deploy/kubernetes/deploy
          BUILD_VARS: ''
        run: |
          SET_ARGS=()
          if [ -n "${BUILD_VARS}" ]; then
            IFS=',' read -ra PAIRS <<< "${BUILD_VARS}"
            for pair in "${PAIRS[@]}"; do
              SET_ARGS+=( --set "${pair}" )
            done
          fi
          pack build \
            --directory "${DEPLOY_DIR}" \
            --recursive \
            --debug \
            "${SET_ARGS[@]}"

      - name: Push overlays
        env:
          DEPLOY_DIR: deploy/kubernetes/deploy
          TAG: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.rev_tag }}
          OCI_USERNAME: ${{ vars.REGISTRY_USERNAME }}
          OCI_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          pack push \
            --directory "${DEPLOY_DIR}" \
            --tag "${TAG}" \
            --recursive \
            --debug

# Kustomize Deployment Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Create a complete Kustomize deployment under `deploy/kubernetes/` with a base layer and a single cluster overlay for `eks-shared-infra-use1-2`.

**Architecture:** Base layer is split into four sub-directories (bootstrap, init, netpol, services) each with their own `kustomization.yaml`. The cluster overlay at `deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/` references the base and applies cluster-specific patches (ingress visibility, service account). All resources share a single container image with command overrides per workload.

**Tech Stack:** Kustomize v4+, Kubernetes manifests (apps/v1, batch/v1, networking.k8s.io/v1), external-secrets.io v1beta1 (ExternalSecret), cilium.io/v2 (CiliumNetworkPolicy)

---

## File Map

**Create — base bootstrap:**
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/namespace.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/serviceaccount.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/secret.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/app-config.env`
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/kustomization.yaml`

**Create — base init:**
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/init/job.yaml`

**Create — base netpol:**
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/allow-dns.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/allow-rds.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/allow-external.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/kustomization.yaml`

**Create — base services:**
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/services/web-deployment.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/services/worker-deployment.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/services/service.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/services/ingress.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/services/kustomization.yaml`

**Create — base root:**
- `deploy/kubernetes/base/kustomization.yaml`

**Create — overlay:**
- `deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/kustomization.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/.app.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/ingress-patch.yaml`
- `deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/serviceaccount.yaml`

---

## Task 1: Bootstrap Resources

Creates the namespace, service account, ExternalSecret, and ConfigMap source.

**Files:**
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/namespace.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/serviceaccount.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/secret.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/app-config.env`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/kustomization.yaml`

- [ ] **Step 1: Create directory structure**

```bash
mkdir -p deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Create namespace.yaml**

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/namespace.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create serviceaccount.yaml**

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/serviceaccount.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast
  namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Create secret.yaml (ExternalSecret)**

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/secret.yaml
apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast
  namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
spec:
  refreshInterval: 1h
  secretStoreRef:
    name: vault
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
  target:
    name: churn-renewal-forecast
    creationPolicy: Owner
  data:
    - secretKey: DATABASE_URL
      remoteRef:
        key: /internal/churn-renewal-forecast
        property: DATABASE_URL
    - secretKey: CLERK_SECRET_KEY
      remoteRef:
        key: /internal/churn-renewal-forecast
        property: CLERK_SECRET_KEY
    - secretKey: FRONT_API_TOKEN
      remoteRef:
        key: /internal/churn-renewal-forecast
        property: FRONT_API_TOKEN
    - secretKey: FRONT_API_TOKEN_2
      remoteRef:
        key: /internal/churn-renewal-forecast
        property: FRONT_API_TOKEN_2
    - secretKey: PRODUCTBOARD_API_KEY
      remoteRef:
        key: /internal/churn-renewal-forecast
        property: PRODUCTBOARD_API_KEY
    - secretKey: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
      remoteRef:
        key: /internal/churn-renewal-forecast
        property: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Create app-config.env**

```env
# deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/app-config.env
APP_URL=https://churn-forecast.infrastructure.immuta.io
NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=PLACEHOLDER
NEXT_PUBLIC_PRODUCTBOARD_WORKSPACE=PLACEHOLDER
SLACK_TEST_CHANNEL=
PG_POOL_MAX=10
PG_POOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=30000
PG_POOL_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS=2000
NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_SIGN_IN_URL=/sign-in
NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_SIGN_UP_URL=/sign-up
NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_AFTER_SIGN_IN_URL=/
NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_AFTER_SIGN_UP_URL=/
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Create bootstrap/kustomization.yaml**

`configMapGenerator` produces the ConfigMap from `app-config.env`. `disableNameSuffixHash: true` keeps the name stable so `envFrom` references don't need to change on every deploy.

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/kustomization.yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - namespace.yaml
  - serviceaccount.yaml
  - secret.yaml

configMapGenerator:
  - name: churn-renewal-forecast-config
    envs:
      - app-config.env

generatorOptions:
  disableNameSuffixHash: true
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Validate bootstrap kustomization builds**

```bash
kustomize build deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap
```

Expected: YAML output containing Namespace, ServiceAccount, ExternalSecret, and ConfigMap. No errors.

- [ ] **Step 8: Commit**

```bash
git add deploy/kubernetes/base/bootstrap/
git commit -m "feat: add k8s bootstrap resources (namespace, sa, secret, configmap)"
```

---

## Task 2: Init Job

Creates the one-shot Prisma migration Job that runs before the app starts.

**Files:**
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/init/job.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/init/kustomization.yaml`

- [ ] **Step 1: Create directory**

```bash
mkdir -p deploy/kubernetes/base/init
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Create job.yaml**

`ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 300` auto-deletes the Job pod 5 minutes after it completes. `backoffLimit: 3` retries up to 3 times on failure. `prisma migrate deploy` is idempotent — safe to re-run.

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/init/job.yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast-migrate
  namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
    app.kubernetes.io/component: migrate
spec:
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 300
  backoffLimit: 3
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
        app.kubernetes.io/component: migrate
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: churn-renewal-forecast
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
      containers:
        - name: migrate
          image: registry.ic-ops.net/churn-renewal-forecast:latest
          command: ["bunx", "prisma", "migrate", "deploy"]
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: churn-renewal-forecast-config
            - secretRef:
                name: churn-renewal-forecast
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create init/kustomization.yaml**

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/init/kustomization.yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - job.yaml
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Validate**

```bash
kustomize build deploy/kubernetes/base/init
```

Expected: YAML output containing a single Job. No errors.

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add deploy/kubernetes/base/init/
git commit -m "feat: add k8s init job for prisma migrations"
```

---

## Task 3: Network Policies

Creates three CiliumNetworkPolicy resources covering DNS, RDS, and external HTTPS egress.

**Files:**
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/allow-dns.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/allow-rds.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/allow-external.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/kustomization.yaml`

- [ ] **Step 1: Create directory**

```bash
mkdir -p deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Create allow-dns.yaml**

Allows pods with `app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast` to reach `kube-dns` on UDP 53. The `rules.dns` section tells Cilium to track DNS responses so FQDN policies in `allow-external.yaml` can resolve correctly.

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/allow-dns.yaml
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast-allow-dns
  namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
  egress:
    - toEndpoints:
        - matchLabels:
            k8s:io.kubernetes.pod.namespace: kube-system
            k8s-app: kube-dns
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "53"
              protocol: UDP
          rules:
            dns:
              - matchPattern: "*"
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create allow-rds.yaml**

Allows outbound TCP 5432 to any IP. Scoped to CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 because RDS runs outside the cluster — you cannot use an endpoint selector for external IPs.

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/allow-rds.yaml
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast-allow-rds
  namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
  egress:
    - toCIDR:
        - 0.0.0.0/0
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "5432"
              protocol: TCP
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Create allow-external.yaml**

`toFQDNs` with `matchName` locks to the exact hostname. `matchPattern: "*.clerk.com"` covers Clerk's subdomains (e.g. `accounts.clerk.com`). `*.slack.com` covers Slack API endpoints. Requires `allow-dns.yaml` to be active so Cilium can resolve these FQDNs.

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/allow-external.yaml
apiVersion: cilium.io/v2
kind: CiliumNetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast-allow-external
  namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
spec:
  endpointSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
  egress:
    - toFQDNs:
        - matchName: "clerk.com"
        - matchPattern: "*.clerk.com"
        - matchName: "api.frontapp.com"
        - matchName: "api.productboard.com"
        - matchName: "slack.com"
        - matchPattern: "*.slack.com"
      toPorts:
        - ports:
            - port: "443"
              protocol: TCP
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Create netpol/kustomization.yaml**

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/kustomization.yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - allow-dns.yaml
  - allow-rds.yaml
  - allow-external.yaml
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Validate**

```bash
kustomize build deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol
```

Expected: YAML output with three CiliumNetworkPolicy resources. No errors.

- [ ] **Step 7: Commit**

```bash
git add deploy/kubernetes/base/netpol/
git commit -m "feat: add cilium network policies (dns, rds, external egress)"
```

---

## Task 4: Services (Deployments, Service, Ingress)

Creates the web Deployment (Next.js), worker Deployment (pg-boss), ClusterIP Service, and Nginx Ingress.

**Files:**
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/services/web-deployment.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/services/worker-deployment.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/services/service.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/services/ingress.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/services/kustomization.yaml`

- [ ] **Step 1: Create directory**

```bash
mkdir -p deploy/kubernetes/base/services
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Create web-deployment.yaml**

`command: ["bun", "run", "start"]` maps to `next start` from the project's `package.json`. Liveness checks `/api/health/live` to detect a hung process; readiness checks `/api/health/ready` to gate traffic until the app is warm.

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/services/web-deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast-web
  namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
    app.kubernetes.io/component: web
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
      app.kubernetes.io/component: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
        app.kubernetes.io/component: web
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: churn-renewal-forecast
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: registry.ic-ops.net/churn-renewal-forecast:latest
          command: ["bun", "run", "start"]
          ports:
            - containerPort: 3000
              name: http
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: churn-renewal-forecast-config
            - secretRef:
                name: churn-renewal-forecast
          resources:
            requests:
              memory: 256Mi
              cpu: 100m
            limits:
              memory: 512Mi
              cpu: 500m
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /api/health/live
              port: 3000
            initialDelaySeconds: 15
            periodSeconds: 20
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /api/health/ready
              port: 3000
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 10
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create worker-deployment.yaml**

`command: ["bunx", "tsx", "src/worker/index.ts"]` maps to `bun run worker` from `package.json`. No HTTP port or probes — the worker is a queue consumer that runs until killed; Kubernetes monitors the process exit code.

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/services/worker-deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast-worker
  namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
    app.kubernetes.io/component: worker
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
      app.kubernetes.io/component: worker
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
        app.kubernetes.io/component: worker
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: churn-renewal-forecast
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: registry.ic-ops.net/churn-renewal-forecast:latest
          command: ["bunx", "tsx", "src/worker/index.ts"]
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: churn-renewal-forecast-config
            - secretRef:
                name: churn-renewal-forecast
          resources:
            requests:
              memory: 256Mi
              cpu: 100m
            limits:
              memory: 512Mi
              cpu: 500m
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Create service.yaml**

ClusterIP routes traffic to web pods only (selector scoped to `component: web`). Port 80 externally → 3000 on the container.

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/services/service.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast
  namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
    app.kubernetes.io/component: web
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
    app.kubernetes.io/component: web
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 3000
      name: http
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Create ingress.yaml**

TLS terminates at the ingress; the `churn-renewal-forecast-tls` secret is managed externally (cert-manager or equivalent). The `ingressClassName` field replaces the deprecated `kubernetes.io/ingress.class` annotation in Kubernetes 1.18+.

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/services/ingress.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast
  namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: churn-renewal-forecast
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  tls:
    - hosts:
        - churn-forecast.infrastructure.immuta.io
      secretName: churn-renewal-forecast-tls
  rules:
    - host: churn-forecast.infrastructure.immuta.io
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: churn-renewal-forecast
                port:
                  name: http
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Create services/kustomization.yaml**

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/services/kustomization.yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - web-deployment.yaml
  - worker-deployment.yaml
  - service.yaml
  - ingress.yaml
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Validate**

```bash
kustomize build deploy/kubernetes/base/services
```

Expected: YAML output with two Deployments, one Service, one Ingress. No errors.

- [ ] **Step 8: Commit**

```bash
git add deploy/kubernetes/base/services/
git commit -m "feat: add k8s service resources (web, worker deployments, svc, ingress)"
```

---

## Task 5: Base Root Kustomization

Ties all four base sub-directories together into a single root kustomization.

**Files:**
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/base/kustomization.yaml`

- [ ] **Step 1: Create base/kustomization.yaml**

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/base/kustomization.yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - bootstrap/
  - init/
  - netpol/
  - services/
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Validate full base build**

```bash
kustomize build deploy/kubernetes/base
```

Expected: Combined YAML output with all resources — Namespace, ServiceAccount, ExternalSecret, ConfigMap, Job, three CiliumNetworkPolicies, two Deployments, Service, Ingress. No errors.

- [ ] **Step 3: Commit**

```bash
git add deploy/kubernetes/base/kustomization.yaml
git commit -m "feat: add k8s base kustomization root"
```

---

## Task 6: Cluster Overlay (eks-shared-infra-use1-2)

Creates the overlay that references the base and applies cluster-specific patches: private ingress visibility and a service account patch stub for optional IRSA.

**Files:**
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/kustomization.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/.app.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/ingress-patch.yaml`
- Create: `deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/serviceaccount.yaml`

- [ ] **Step 1: Create directory**

```bash
mkdir -p deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Create .app.yaml**

Flux metadata file consumed by the cluster's GitOps tooling. Update the `cluster` field if the cluster name differs.

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/.app.yaml
app: churn-renewal-forecast
namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
cluster: eks-shared-infra-use1-2
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create ingress-patch.yaml**

Strategic merge patch that adds the internal-load-balancer annotation to the base Ingress. This restricts the ALB to private subnets only.

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/ingress-patch.yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast
  namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-internal: "true"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/scheme: internal
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Create serviceaccount.yaml**

Strategic merge patch stub. The IRSA annotation is commented out because this app does not need AWS API access. Uncomment and supply the role ARN if that changes.

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/serviceaccount.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: churn-renewal-forecast
  namespace: churn-renewal-forecast
  # annotations:
  #   eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/churn-renewal-forecast
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Create overlay kustomization.yaml**

```yaml
# deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2/kustomization.yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - ../../base

patches:
  - path: ingress-patch.yaml
  - path: serviceaccount.yaml
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Validate full overlay build**

This is the final validation — it produces the exact manifests that would be applied to the cluster.

```bash
kustomize build deploy/kubernetes/deploy/eks-shared-infra-use1-2
```

Expected: All base resources with the Ingress now carrying both `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-internal: "true"` and `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/scheme: internal` annotations. No errors.

- [ ] **Step 7: Commit**

```bash
git add deploy/kubernetes/deploy/
git commit -m "feat: add eks-shared-infra-use1-2 overlay (private ingress, sa stub)"
```

---

234			}

Clear picture now. The issue is:

- `deps` stage: `bun install --production --ignore-scripts` → skips `@prisma/engines` postinstall, so the schema engine binary is never downloaded
- `runner` stage: copies `node_modules` from `deps` → schema engine binary is missing
- At runtime in the Kubernetes job, `prisma migrate deploy` tries to fetch it from `binaries.prisma.sh` → blocked by network policy

The fix is one line in the Dockerfile runner stage: copy `@prisma/engines` from the `build` stage (where `bun install` ran scripts and the binary was downloaded) on top of the production node_modules.

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client"
  output   = "../src/generated/prisma"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
}

enum GlobalRole {
  ADMIN
  MANAGER
  USER
}

enum CustomerRole {
  CSM  // Customer Success Manager
  AE   // Account Executive
  SA   // Sales Engineer
  FCTO // Field CTO
  RSA  // RSA
}

model User {
  id              String             @id @default(cuid())
  name            String?
  email           String             @unique
  image           String?

  // Clerk integration
  clerkUserId     String?            @unique

  // Link to Person for customer assignments
  personId        String?            @unique
  person          Person?            @relation("PersonUser", fields: [personId], references: [id])

  // Permissions
  globalRole      GlobalRole         @default(USER)
  isDeprovisioned Boolean            @default(false)
  deprovisionedAt DateTime?

  // Relations
  forecasts       ContractForecast[] // Official forecasts

  // Background sync jobs
  syncJobs        SyncJob[]

  // Notification reads
  notificationReads NotificationRead[]

  createdAt       DateTime           @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime           @updatedAt
}

// Anyone who can be assigned to customers (may or may not have login)
model Person {
  id          String               @id @default(cuid())
  email       String               @unique
  displayName String
  createdAt   DateTime             @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime             @updatedAt

  // Optional login account
  user        User?                @relation("PersonUser")

  // Customer assignments
  assignments CustomerAssignment[]
}

// Links Person to Customer with a role
model CustomerAssignment {
  id         String       @id @default(cuid())
  personId   String
  person     Person       @relation(fields: [personId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  customerId String
  customer   Customer     @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  role       CustomerRole
  createdAt  DateTime     @default(now())

  @@unique([personId, customerId, role]) // Person can have multiple roles per customer
  @@index([personId])
  @@index([customerId])
}

enum ForecastStatus {
  CLOSED_LOST
  NOTIFIED_CHURN
  EXPECTING_CHURN
  CLOSED_WON
  EXPECTING_RENEW
  AT_RISK
}

enum ContractStatus {
  OPEN
  RENEWED_FLAT
  RENEWED_EXPANSION
  RENEWED_CONTRACTION
  CHURNED
}

enum Region {
  APJ
  EMEA
  US_WEST
  US_EAST
  PUBLIC_SECTOR
}

enum SkuCategory {
  CONNECTOR             // All connectors (individual + bundles)
  USER                  // User licenses (USR-*, PROD-USER-LICENSE-*)
  SUPPORT               // Support tiers (SUP-*, SERVICES-SUPPORT-*)
  PROFESSIONAL_SERVICES // RSA services
  OTHER                 // IMM-*, IMP-*, discounts, misc
}

enum SkuStatus {
  ACTIVE   // Available for sale
  INACTIVE // No longer sold
}

model Customer {
  id                    String               @id @default(cuid())
  name                  String
  region                Region?
  saasCustomer          Boolean
  productboardCompanyId String?              @unique // Linked Productboard company ID
  productboardCompany   ProductboardCompany? @relation(fields: [productboardCompanyId], references: [id])
  frontAccountId        String?              @unique // Linked Front account ID
  frontAccount          FrontAccount?        @relation(fields: [frontAccountId], references: [id])
  createdAt             DateTime             @default(now())
  updatedAt             DateTime             @updatedAt
  contracts             Contract[]

  // Customer assignments for permission scoping
  assignments           CustomerAssignment[]

  // Consumption tracking
  consumptionSnapshots  CustomerConsumption[]
  usageSnapshots        CustomerUsageSnapshot[]

  // Successor relationship: when a customer splits/rebrands and continues under a new name
  successorId           String?
  successor             Customer?  @relation("CustomerSuccessor", fields: [successorId], references: [id])
  predecessors          Customer[] @relation("CustomerSuccessor")

  // Notifications
  notifications         Notification[]

  // Notification suppression window
  suppressNotificationsUntil DateTime?

  // Slack channel assignment
  slackChannelId        String?   // Stable Slack channel ID (e.g., C01234567)
  slackChannelName      String?   // Display name cached at link time (e.g., deployment-acme)

  // Per-customer sync jobs
  syncJobs              SyncJob[]

  @@index([successorId])
}

model Contract {
  id               String             @id @default(cuid())
  customerId       String
  customer         Customer           @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  arr              Float              // Contract ARR
  startDate        DateTime
  overwriteStartDate          DateTime?  // Override for start date
  endDate          DateTime           // Original contract renewal date
  overwriteEndDate            DateTime?  // Override for early churn recognition
  overwriteDateComment        String?    @map("overwriteEndDateComment") // Reason for overriding dates
  countAgainstOriginalEndDate Boolean?   // When true, dashboard chart/table uses original endDate instead of overwriteEndDate
  contractStatus   ContractStatus     @default(OPEN)             // Actual outcome (fact)
  forecasts        ContractForecast[] // Multiple forecasts over time (official)
  lineItems        ContractLineItem[] // Contract line items (SKU/pricing details)

  // CSM compensation: whether this contract counts towards expansion target
  countsTowardsExpansionTarget   Boolean   @default(true)
  expansionTargetReason          String?   // Required explanation when changed from default

  // ARR exclusion: flag contracts that should be invisible to all ARR calculations
  excludeFromArr                 Boolean   @default(false)
  excludeFromArrReason           String?   // Required explanation when flag is true

  createdAt        DateTime           @default(now())
  updatedAt        DateTime           @updatedAt

  @@index([customerId])
  @@index([endDate])
  @@index([overwriteStartDate])
  @@index([overwriteEndDate])
  @@index([contractStatus])
  @@index([contractStatus, excludeFromArr, overwriteStartDate]) // covers OPEN-only ARR rollup CTEs
  @@index([contractStatus, overwriteEndDate]) // covers overdue/upcoming contract sorts
}

model ContractForecast {
  id           String                  @id @default(cuid())
  contractId   String
  contract     Contract                @relation(fields: [contractId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  createdById  String                  // Link to User who created this forecast
  createdBy    User                    @relation(fields: [createdById], references: [id])
  forecastedAt DateTime                @default(now()) // When forecast was created
  notes        String?
  entries      ContractForecastEntry[]

  @@index([contractId])
  @@index([contractId, forecastedAt(sort: Desc)]) // covers "latest forecast per contract" correlated subqueries
  @@index([forecastedAt])
  @@index([createdById])
}

model ContractForecastEntry {
  id         String           @id @default(cuid())
  forecastId String
  forecast   ContractForecast @relation(fields: [forecastId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  status     ForecastStatus   // CLOSED_WON, EXPECTING_RENEW, AT_RISK, etc.
  arr        Float            // Amount of contract ARR in this status

  @@unique([forecastId, status]) // One entry per status per forecast
  @@index([forecastId, status]) // Composite index for forecast status filters
}

model ProductboardCompany {
  id        String              @id // Productboard's company ID
  name      String
  domain    String?
  customers Customer[]
  notes     ProductboardNote[]
  syncedAt  DateTime            @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime            @updatedAt
}

model ProductboardNote {
  id          String    @id // Productboard's note ID
  title       String?
  content     String?   @db.Text
  displayUrl  String?
  state       String?   // processed, unprocessed, etc.
  tags        String[]  // Array of tag names
  ownerEmail  String?   // User who submitted the note
  ownerName   String?
  createdById String?   // Productboard user ID who created the note
  createdByName  String?
  createdByEmail String?
  createdAt   DateTime
  updatedAt   DateTime?
  syncedAt    DateTime  @default(now())

  // Link to Productboard company
  productboardCompanyId String?
  productboardCompany   ProductboardCompany? @relation(fields: [productboardCompanyId], references: [id])

  // Feature links
  features ProductboardNoteFeature[]

  @@index([productboardCompanyId])
  @@index([createdAt])
}

model ProductboardFeature {
  id              String    @id // Productboard feature/component ID
  name            String?
  status          String?
  isComponent     Boolean   @default(false)
  parentFeatureId String?   // plain string, no FK — parent may not be in our graph

  syncedAt  DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  noteLinks ProductboardNoteFeature[]

  @@index([parentFeatureId])
  @@index([isComponent])
}

model ProductboardNoteFeature {
  id        String              @id @default(cuid())
  noteId    String
  note      ProductboardNote    @relation(fields: [noteId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  featureId String
  feature   ProductboardFeature @relation(fields: [featureId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([noteId, featureId])
  @@index([featureId])
}

// ============================================
// CONSUMPTION & SKU TRACKING
// ============================================

// Daily consumption snapshot for a customer
model CustomerConsumption {
  id              String   @id @default(cuid())
  customerId      String
  customer        Customer @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  // Consumption values
  dataSources     Int      // Number of data sources connected
  registeredUsers Int      // Total registered users
  policies        Int      // Number of policies configured
  activeUsers31d  Int      // Users active in last 31 days
  activeUsersDaily   Int?  // Users active in last 1 day
  activeUsers90d     Int?  // Users active in last 90 days
  activeUsersYearly  Int?  // Users active in last 365 days

  // User breakdown
  policyOwners    Int @default(0)  // Policy Owners / Governors
  dataConsumers   Int @default(0)  // Data Consumers

  // Policy breakdown
  dataPolicies         Int @default(0)  // Data Policies
  subscriptionPolicies Int @default(0)  // Subscription Policies

  snapshotDate    DateTime @db.Date
  createdAt       DateTime @default(now())

  @@unique([customerId, snapshotDate])
  @@index([customerId])
  @@index([snapshotDate])
  @@index([customerId, snapshotDate])
}

// Per-customer PBAC usage snapshot (from the usage metrics CSV)
model CustomerUsageSnapshot {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  customerId   String
  customer     Customer @relation(fields: [customerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  snapshotDate DateTime @db.Date @default(now())

  dataSources                       Int @default(0)
  subscriptionPolicies              Int @default(0)
  guardrailPolicies                 Int @default(0)
  dataPolicies                      Int @default(0)
  users                             Int @default(0)
  samlIntegrations                  Int @default(0)
  scimIntegrations                  Int @default(0)
  dataSourcesWithDataPolicy         Int @default(0)
  dataSourcesWithSubscriptionPolicy Int @default(0)
  tags                              Int @default(0)
  domains                           Int @default(0)
  domainsWithDataSources            Int @default(0)
  domainPolicies                    Int @default(0)

  @@unique([customerId, snapshotDate])
  @@index([customerId])
}

// Master SKU catalog
model Sku {
  id               String      @id @default(cuid())
  code             String      @unique  // e.g., "USR-PWR"
  name             String               // Human-readable name
  description      String?
  category         SkuCategory
  status           SkuStatus   @default(ACTIVE)
  listPrice        Float?
  createdAt        DateTime    @default(now())
  updatedAt        DateTime    @updatedAt
  lineItems        ContractLineItem[]

  // SKU replacement tracking (e.g., USR-DC replaced by USR-PWR)
  replacedById     String?     @unique
  replacedBy       Sku?        @relation("SkuReplacement", fields: [replacedById], references: [id])
  replaces         Sku?        @relation("SkuReplacement")

  @@index([category])
  @@index([status])
}

// Contract line items
model ContractLineItem {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  contractId String
  contract   Contract @relation(fields: [contractId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  skuId      String
  sku        Sku      @relation(fields: [skuId], references: [id])

  // Pricing
  listPrice  Float    // List price per unit at time of sale
  discount   Float    // Discount percentage (0-100)
  unitPrice  Float    // Actual price per unit after discount
  quantity   Int      // Number of units purchased
  totalPrice Float    // Total price (unitPrice * quantity)

  // Line item period dates (inherited from contract for single-year contracts)
  startDate  DateTime
  endDate    DateTime

  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt

  // Note: No unique constraint - same SKU can appear multiple times per contract
  // (e.g., multiple amendments, tiers, or pricing structures)
  @@index([contractId])
  @@index([skuId])
}

// ============================================
// FRONT APP INTEGRATION
// ============================================

model FrontAccount {
